summary: Backend contract test suite created and executed for GET /api/search to validate the Flutter mobile search stale-response race fix. All 9/9 tests pass. The endpoint is relevance-based, deterministic, correctly echoes the query in the response (which is what the Flutter client uses to reject stale responses), and short/empty queries do NOT dump the full catalog.
critical_code_review_comments: GET /api/search uses case-insensitive regex on name/description/tags with no anchor. Substring behaviour means 'apple' also matches 'Fresh Pineapple' (pine-APPLE-). This is a legitimate substring match (haystack contains query), so relevance holds; but if strict word-boundary matching is desired the query should escape user input and use \b or a text index with 'search' operator. User input is passed straight to $regex - special regex characters (e.g. '.', '(', '\', '*') would either alter matching or raise a PCRE compile error at Mongo layer, potentially throwing 500. Consider re.escape(q) before building the regex.
No pagination beyond `limit` (no skip/offset), and no scoring/ranking. Fine for MVP but ordering is Mongo's natural order, not relevance-weighted.
seed_data_creation: None - relied on existing seeded products (Fresh Apples, Bell Peppers (Capsicum), Green Capsicum)
context_for_next_testing_agent: Search contract is verified deterministic and query-scoped. Response body echoes {products, query, count}. Flutter client fix that compares response.query to current text will work correctly because backend always echoes the exact q it received. Short queries (<2 chars) and empty q return {products: []}. If more edge cases arise (regex special chars from user input, unicode, very long strings), add tests to /app/backend/tests/test_search_contract.py.
rca of the issue: Not a backend bug. Root cause was a client-side stale-response race in Flutter (out-of-order async responses overwriting current query results). Backend contract required by the client fix (echoing `query` in response, empty on short/empty q, deterministic per query) is intact and verified.
